# Native Muscle Experiment Bundle

## Scope and State Authority

F07d #11908 connects the merged Tools `ExperimentReplayBundle` authority to
the existing OpenSim native muscle excitation replay kernel. It does not add
an integrator, muscle law, or acceptance evaluator. Initial admission is a
reviewed cold-start subset with Millard and Thelen equilibrium muscles, fixed path
points, Slider/Pin joints, muscle forces and gravity. Constraints, locks,
clamps, moving points, contact, other forces, plugins and unreviewed concrete
components remain excluded. All excluded engines and production variants
remain in the required parity denominator.

Every named continuous state must be supplied without defaults or muscle
equilibration. Native continuous `Y` coverage is checked, but does not prove
complete SimTK State serialization. Scalar actuators allocate discrete
override force and an override modeling option; muscles also allocate
activation/tendon modeling options. Coordinate clamp options are likewise
distinct from continuous state. Registered discrete-variable and modeling-option
path/value sets are included as auxiliary bundle state, together with force
enabled/override and muscle-mode flags. Fresh initialization must reproduce
these values exactly. Unsupported private subsystem or abstract state remains
outside this policy, rather than being reported as absent or zero.

The primary native source review is
[Actuator.cpp](https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/blob/85aaf6450a2f22457dac4d1ab35adfed9d3a8e43/OpenSim/Simulation/Model/Actuator.cpp),
[Muscle.cpp](https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/blob/85aaf6450a2f22457dac4d1ab35adfed9d3a8e43/OpenSim/Simulation/Model/Muscle.cpp), and
[Component.cpp](https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/blob/85aaf6450a2f22457dac4d1ab35adfed9d3a8e43/OpenSim/Common/Component.cpp).
The recorded binary build identifies its runtime separately; reviewing source
does not attest source-to-binary equivalence or transitive library closure.

## Input and Execution

Saved dimensionless excitation is bounded in $[0,1]$ and linearly interpolated
by the existing time-only native player. It is not muscle force or joint
torque. Activation and compliant fiber dynamics remain in the native plant.
All input times are finite, increasing simulation-relative seconds beginning
at zero. Adaptive Runge--Kutta--Merson uses the fixed policy accuracy $10^{-8}$.
A fresh model and Manager execute the full horizon without observations,
feedback callbacks, state corrections or re-equilibration after restoration.

Source bytes, loaded model XML, native runtime/build, executed adapter/kernel,
shared admission helper, native extension binaries, ordered muscle channels,
state schema, initial values and execution/input policies are bound. Bundle
serialization and required capabilities are revalidated before execution.
Provider hashing is scoped evidence, not a process sandbox or full DLL
dependency attestation. Execution requires exclusive native process ownership.

## Evidence and Remaining Gates

Commit `a8e63b4cda` records six native missing-module RED tests before the
implementation. Subsequent law and admission negatives were recorded before
their fixes. Actual OpenSim4.6 validation passes 26 bundle and 58 kernel tests
across both muscle laws, checking fresh
continuous-state reproduction, native excitation readback, explicit registered
options, missing fiber rejection, changed source rejection, and an unreviewed
force rejection. Self-contained XML admission rejects external resources
before native loading; required owned capabilities cannot be replaced. These
are synthetic development fixtures only. The source-byte ownership and explicit-unit regressions also pass. Scoped
mypy, all five central gates, DRY, LoD, architecture, canonical governance and
generated-context checks pass. After genuine contact-parent integration,134 actual native tests pass with
two inapplicable contact-fixture skips. Shared kernel policy1.3.1 combines
exact concrete-law admission with listed native-contact identity. The bundle
subset continues to exclude contact. All five final central gates pass. Derivative/force initialization audits and publication
remain pending at this checkpoint.

The 520-muscle candidate has locked coordinates, couplers and non-muscle
actuators and is not admitted by this policy. Native position geometry and
marker fitting are separate from dynamics qualification. Full-body anatomy,
frame registration, physiological/passive-force feasibility, contact and grip,
training-only calibration, heldout accuracy, uninterrupted muscle-driven
capture replay and all-engine/model parity remain open.

## Assistance-Explicit Scalar Replay

Child #12147 adds a separate mixed profile in
`tour_matching/native_mixed_actuation.py` and `native_mixed_replay.py`.
The original muscle-only admission remains strict. This first mixed subset
admits the same fixed-path equilibrium muscle laws and Slider/Pin topology,
plus exact native `CoordinateActuator` instances. Constraints, moving/wrapped
paths, contact, prescribed motion and other concrete components remain outside
this profile. It does not yet admit the complete Rajagopal or 520-muscle model.

Each ordered channel has an absolute native component path, an explicit role,
and finite closed experimental control bounds inside the native bounds.
Point bounds permit an exactly zero mechanical-assistance ablation. Muscles
retain native activation and compliant tendon dynamics; their dimensionless
input is excitation. Mechanical commands are dimensionless scalar inputs,
with native actuation $f_i=u_i f_{i,\mathrm{optimal}}$. For rotational
coordinates this output is N m; for translation it is N. The T01 input kind is
`ACTUATOR_COMMAND`, with `LINEAR` interpolation, because channels have mixed
physical meanings. It is not a vector of joint torques or muscle forces.

A mechanical actuator on a joint whose parent base frame is ground must be
reported as root residual assistance, regardless of actuator or coordinate
names. Other upper-assistance and leg-reserve roles are explicit experimental
region declarations, not validated anatomical classifications. Full native
actuator coverage and order, gains, motion units, force enable/override,
muscle modes, and default and live coordinate restrictions are checked.
Registered override auxiliary state inherits its owning scalar actuator's
output units. No missing physical state is filled or equilibrated on replay.

The profile digest binds declared roles/bounds and actual native readback.
Source XML, loaded native model, T01 complete named state and registered
options, saved controls, policy, runtime extensions and executed helper source
are revalidated before a fresh replay. Native extension discovery must be
nonempty independently of the Python helper count. The shared engine-owned
`native_scalar_replay` executor uses one Manager, exact returned physical time,
and sampled native control readback. Every returned applied control must
match the saved ordered history within absolute tolerance $10^{-12}$.
No observation access, feedback, correction or Manager restart is permitted.

Returned histories include native actuation, native actuator power $P_i$,
and cumulative sampled trapezoidal work:
$$
W_i(t_k)=\sum_{j=1}^{k}\frac{P_i(t_{j-1})+P_i(t_j)}{2}
(t_j-t_{j-1}).
$$
For a CoordinateActuator, $P_i=f_i\dot q_i$ with the matching force/torque
units. Muscle power is the native actuator output and must not be interpreted
as total metabolic or complete elastic storage energy. Work is output-grid
quadrature, not a qualified energy balance; refinement is required for
scientific comparisons. Returned arrays are immutable owned byte-backed
samples, with source, provider, input, initial-state and execution-policy
digests. Assistance forces, powers and work remain separately labeled by
channel role; disabling a channel does not remove it from the accounting.

Actual native synthetic tests cover signed assistance, gain and unit readback,
misleading names and renamed ground coordinates, live lock/clamp/prescription,
fixed-zero ablations, serialization and fresh deterministic replay, changed
future inputs, immutable result storage, changed source/roles/bounds/gain,
missing state/channels, unavailable native binaries, actual player mismatch,
and a mislabeled native initial time. The legacy muscle/contact/Moco regression
also runs after extracting the common integration loop. These fixtures do not
establish full-horizon capture matching, anatomical correspondence, ground
support, muscle physiology, contact/grip, or all 17 production-variant parity.
